description_full: Idaho Strategic Resources, Inc., a resource-based company, engages in the exploration, development, and extraction of gold, silver, and base metal mineral resources in the North Idaho. The company was formerly known as New Jersey Mining Company and changed its name to Idaho Strategic Resources, Inc. in December 2021. Idaho Strategic Resources, Inc. was incorporated in 1996 and is based in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho.

financial_summary: Idaho Strategic Resources, Inc. is a small-cap basic materials business with a $330M market cap on $42M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +64% over the past three years and +36% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 16% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $12M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.14× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.1× net debt/EBITDA.

Net dilution runs at 15.8% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 5.6% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
